item.title: MiLaysia Fulwiley scores 14 in return as No. 9 LSU cruises past Belmont 103-45
item.description: 23 MiLaysia Fulwiley, LSU Tigers Womens Basketball take on the Belmont Bruins. November 23, 2026; Baton Rouge, LA; at the Pete Maravich Assembly Center USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect BATON ROUGE, La. (AP) — LSU senior guard MiLaysia Fulwiley returned to play Monday following a two-game absence because of an arrest and scored 14 points in the No. 9 Lady Tigers’ 103-45 victory over Belmont. Fulwiley was a starter in LSU’s first four games until her Nov. 9 arrest for allegedly attempting to flee a traffic stop. The two most serious charges — aggravated battery and aggravated assault — were dropped last Friday by Baton Rouge District Attorney Hillar Moore, and Fulwiley will enter a pre-trial diversion program to have the remaining charges of flight from an officer, resisting an officer and obedience to officers dropped. Senior guard Mikaylah Williams had eight of her team-high 20 points in the fourth quarter to help LSU (7-0) complete its season-opening, seven-game homestand. The Lady Tigers scored the first 23 points in the final quarter and led 96-35 on Lola Lampley’s free throw with 4:18 left. LSU also received double-figure scoring from Grace Knox (14), ZaKiyah Johnson (14), and Lampley (13). Fulwiley, who drew an ovation from the crowd, entered the game with 4:37 left in the first quarter and LSU in the midst of a 13-0 run to begin the game. She hit her first shot – a 3-pointer from the wing – less than a minute after entering game and followed with a layup to complete a fastbreak opportunity. Fulwiley played 17 minutes, made 6 of 13 shots and had a team-high five steals. Belmont’s first points of the game were courtesy of Chelby Jordan’s 17-foot jumper to end a 0 of 11 shooting streak. Kinley McCarn led the Bruins (1-6) with a game-high 25 points, including seven of her team’s 12 3-pointers. Up next LSU: Vs. Villanova in the Ft. Myers Tip Off on Friday. Belmont: Vs. Iowa State in the Baha Mar Hoops Championship, Nassau, Bahamas on Friday.

item.title: Did Commanders commit penalty on Daniels' spike of ball before FG?
item.description: Officials appeared to miss a penalty on Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels' spike of the ball, just before Drew Stevens' game-winning field goal in the Cincinnati Bengals ' NFL Week 11 loss at Northwest Stadium on ESPN's Monday Night Football. At least seven offensive players must line up on the line of scrimmage before the ball is snapped. As @wvcoachpence pointed out on Twitter/X , Washington "didn't have enough players on the line." A screengrab of the play shows the Commanders have six players on the line of scrimmage. "Should have been a penalty and a ten second run off," @wvcoachpence added. "Wouldn’t have been a fun way to win like that, but still would have been a win." In addition, MNF rules analyst Russell Yurk pointed out just after the game ended that the clock operator should have stopped the clock with two seconds left when Stevens' field goal hit the net. This article originally appeared on Cincinnati Enquirer: Did Commanders commit penalty on Daniels' spike of ball before FG?

This was only the 76ers’ fourth loss of the season, and while this defeat at home was humbling, especially in their first matchup against a Western Conference team, they have plenty of reasons to be optimistic moving forward. item.title: A key component for Manchester City is available for Napoli clash
item.description: A key component for Manchester City is available for Napoli clash Up next for Manchester City is their fifth UEFA Champions League league phase fixture tonight against Napoli at the Etihad Stadium. Enzo Maresca’s side have won three of their first four matches in the competition. Tonight’s match does represent an opportunity for them to take a big step towards a crucial top-eight finish in the UEFA Champions League league phase table. Enzo Maresca revealed yesterday that Manchester City had received a big boost ahead of tonight’s with a key component of City’s defence available for tonight’s clash with Napoli. Manchester City have Matheus Nunes available to play against Napoli. Matheus Nunes missed Manchester City’s 1-1 draw with Fulham due to injury. Speaking yesterday, Enzo Maresca revealed that the Portuguese international is available for tonight’s clash with Napoli. Maresca also revealed that Antoine Semenyo is unavailable for tonight’s match. Furthermore, he added that a selection of Manchester City players are battling fatigue after a heavy workload for both club and country. Maresca explained: “ Matheus is back. The only one out is still Antoine. The rest we have some doubt, in terms of tightness, amount of games. We have today’s session and then we will decide. ” “ It’s normal with the amount of games that we have. That’s why I sometimes rotate players. “ “ We need to think not about sprints but marathons – 65 games. “ “ I would like to use the strongest ones in every game. Then we would destroy them so it’s about managing them in the best way. “ How Enzo Maresca sets up his team’s defence will be worth keeping an eye on tonight. Enzo Maresca is still searching for what is the ideal balance for the Manchester City defence. Teething issues were to be expected as Maresca embeds his ideas and philosophy into his team. Throughout this season, Abdukodir Khusanov and Rico Lewis have slotted in at right-back when Matheus Nunes has been injured. Having Matheus Nunes back does shore up the right-back position for Manchester City. However Maresca constructs his defence around Nunes remains to be seen. Perhaps, it is time for Enzo Maresca to slide Josko Gvardiol across to centre-back to help with his team’s play out from the back. Playing Gvardiol alongside one of Ruben Dias, Marc Guehi or Abdukodir Khusanov should help in this regard. That would require Nico O’Reilly to slot in at left-back with Matheus Nunes at right-back but you do feel that Gvardiol at centre-back could unlock a key piece of Manchester City’s play. Matheus Nunes is back available for Manchester City when they take on Napoli tonight at the Etihad Stadium. That is welcome news for City who are an infinitely stronger team when Nunes slots in at right-back.

item.title: Did LSU pay Bryce Underwood in high school? Martindale was told yes
item.description: The University of Michigan would owe LSU $1.5 million when it flipped Bryce Underwood's commitment to the Wolverines to reimburse the SEC school for what it paid the quarterback in high school, the UM coaching staff was told. That's according to former Michigan defensive coordinator Don “Wink” Martindale, who decried the state of college football in the most recent Family Business Podcast with former NFL coach Norv Turner, his daughter, filmmaker and football insider Stephanie Turner and son, Scott. Martindale served as Michigan's defensive coordinator under head coach Sherrone Moore during the 2024 and 2025 seasons, including the fall 2024 recruiting push in which the Wolverines sought to flip Underwood's commitment from LSU. He said that Moore discussed LSU's payments to Underwood during a staff meeting. What Martindale said about Bryce Underwood "The head coach said, 'We have to pay LSU $1.5 (million) because they've been paying this kid since he was a sophomore in high school," Martindale said. Martindale did not profess to know who was going to pay the money, to whom payment would be made or whether a transaction ever took place. He also said he didn't know how much Underwood was being paid at Michigan under Name, Image and Likeness (NIL) rules, although reports have put it at $10.5 million over four years. NCAA rules prohibit colleges from offering prospective athletes payments or benefits to induce enrollment. Division I Bylaws 13.2.1 and 22.01.2 specifically prohibit recruiting inducements, including the use of name, image and likeness (NIL) compensation to influence a recruit's college choice. Martindale said he shook his head after Moore discussed the payments and questioned how a teenager receiving millions of dollars could be held accountable for his academic responsibilities. "I said, 'Look ... who's gonna make this kid go to class?'" Martindale said on the podcast. Spokespersons from Michigan and LSU, including representatives for the universities' athletic departments, didn't immediately respond to requests for comment. 'It's just not the same' Underwood, a former standout at Belleville High School and the nation's top-ranked recruit in the 2025 class, had been committed to LSU since January 2024 before changing course and choosing Michigan that November. Martindale was on staff when Underwood flipped, but departed after Moore's firing. The Wolverines reportedly put together an NIL deal worth approximately $10.5 million over four years to land the quarterback, who had emerged as one of the most coveted prospects in the country. Underwood picked the Wolverines after LSU had offered him approximately $1.5 million per year in NIL compensation, The Sporting News reported. Martindale predicted that with the current path of college sports, the universities will run out of money to pay players. item.title: ‘(Jayden Daniels) and (Stefon) Diggs For Sure Got Beef’ — Super Bowl Champ Sees Fracture In Relationship Between Commanders Stars
item.description: Washington Commanders wide receiver Stefon Diggs (3) celebrates after a play during the game against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium. Monday Night Football has a way of putting every sideline under a microscope, and the Washington Commanders’ bench got the full treatment against the Cincinnati Bengals. With Washington’s offense stuck in neutral and about four minutes left in the second quarter, ESPN’s broadcast caught Stefon Diggs shouting, “Hey, throw the [expletive] ball!” Diggs had yet to catch a pass at that point, and Darius Slay, the veteran cornerback who earned a Super Bowl ring with the Philadelphia Eagles, appeared to read the moment as a sign of trouble between Diggs and his quarterback. Darius Slay Sees Friction Between Stefon Diggs and Jayden Daniels Slay wrote Monday night: “JD and Diggs for sure got beef!” Daniels had thrown Diggs’ way only once before then, an incompletion on third-and-9 on Washington’s first possession. The Bengals led 3-0 at that point, and Washington had punted on each of its first four possessions. The last was a three-play series that gained 1 yard, coming right after Evan McPherson’s 38-yard field goal opened the scoring. Diggs entered Monday leading Washington with 386 receiving yards on 36 catches and 59 targets, and his six touchdown receptions were tied for eighth in the NFL, with a score in three of his previous four games. Daniels, meanwhile, went into halftime 8-of-11 for 85 yards. Boye Mafe had already sacked him three times, and the Commanders had managed 120 total yards while dealing with offensive miscues in the rain. After a field goal put the Bengals up with 46 seconds left in the contest, Daniels connected with Antonio Williams to pull Washington within field goal range with mere seconds left. That resulting field goal sealed the win, which was the first time the Commanders picked up two wins on the bounce since 2024. Interestingly, Daniels and Diggs had won Washington’s previous game together in the final minute. In that 24-21 victory over the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium on Nov. 12, Daniels hit Diggs for the go-ahead 32-yard touchdown with 57 seconds left. Diggs had six catches for 83 yards that night. In Week 11 Monday night, Diggs finished with four receptions for 45 yards on six targets. On the other hand, Williams had nine catches for 122 receiving yards. He had 93 receiving yards in the fourth quarter alone, the most by any rookie in a game since 2020. Only Drake London (124 in Week 3) and Malik Nabers (102 in Week 6) had more in a game this season. The Commanders, who left Monday night 4-5-1 and third in the NFC East, head to State Farm Stadium next for a Week 12 meeting with the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 4:25 p.m.

item.title: Giant Study Finds Ice Baths Can Relieve Sore Muscles – But There's a Hidden Cost
item.description: (Marc Serota Collection/iStockphoto/Getty Images) Cold water can do some amazing things to the human body , and the fitness world has taken notice. Ice baths – also known as cold water immersion – have been a popular fitness and wellness trend in recent years, with many athletes and enthusiasts embracing cold plunging, in the belief that it can accelerate muscle recovery and boost athletic performance. But do ice baths really work? A giant new review in Sports Medicine – Open might well be the most comprehensive assessment of cold water immersion to date, and it suggests cold plunging does have health benefits for athletes – but those benefits come with some caveats too. "Cold-water immersion is not a one-size-fits-all recovery tool," says lead author and exercise researcher Erfan Berjisian from Edith Cowan University (ECU) in Australia. "Its benefits depend heavily on the athlete's goals, the type of exercise completed, and when the next performance session is scheduled." Ice baths have been used by athletes for decades, but are they effective? (Ivan Rodriguez Alba/Getty Images Signature/Canva) In the study, Berjisian and fellow researchers undertook an umbrella review of scientific literature on ice baths, examining 15 published reviews and meta-analyses, which covered 161 individual studies and 3,210 participants. While that huge body of research measured lots of different things in lots of different ways – and not all of the studies were of necessarily equal quality – in broad terms, the evidence consistently suggests that post-exercise cold water immersion reduces muscle soreness. Ice baths can provide relief from soreness after exercise for up to four days, the findings suggest, with the greatest benefits after high-intensity exercise. But the benefits go beyond how your muscles feel. The researchers also found that cold-water immersion reduces levels of creatine kinase in the bloodstream, which is a marker of muscle damage, with the effects evident from about 24 hours to 72 hours. Ice baths also appear to help the nervous system return to its resting state more quickly after exercise, with cold-water immersion producing improvements in heart-rate variability, although the researchers found no consistent reductions in two key markers of inflammation. As for actual athletic performance, the benefits are more complicated, and depend largely on timing. Cold-water immersion appears to temporarily improve endurance performance, but only if athletes do exercise straight away – within the first hour after immersion – with the benefits generally disappearing after that. For some athletes, that tight timeframe might be advantageous though. item.title: Cubs signing Trevor Rogers to five year, $120 million contract
item.description: Trevor Rogers #28 of the Baltimore Orioles pitches against the Milwaukee Brewers at Oriole Park at Camden Yards on September 19, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. The Cubs have added to their starting rotation. Left-hander Trevor Rogers has agreed to a contract with the Cubs, according to multiple reports. The deal brings Rogers to the Windy City for five years, $120 million, pending a physical, The Athletic’s Ken Rosenthal reported late Monday night. ESPN’s Jeff Passan reported that there are deferrals that will bring down the net present value. Trevor Rogers, who agreed to a deal with the Cubs on Monday, pitches against the Milwaukee Brewers at Oriole Park at Camden Yards on September 19, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. Getty Images Rogers will join a starting rotation that is expected to include Justin Steele, Edward Cabrera, Braxton Garrett and Javier Assad. Rogers is coming off a season in which he had career-bests in starts (30), innings (169 ⅔) and strikeout-to-walk ratio (4.03). The lefty also tied his career-high with 157 strikeouts during the 2026 campaign. He finished the season with a 4.03 ERA. It was a stark difference from the way that the season started for Rogers, who carried a 6.84 ERA in the month of June before quickly turning things around through the remainder of the year. From June 1 on, he posted a 2.90 ERA. Rogers started his career with the Marlins, and in 2021, he finished as the runner-up for NL Rookie of the Year after recording a 2.64 ERA and 157 strikeouts over 133 innings that season. He struggled to replicate the success consistently and was traded to the Orioles during the 2024 season before having an impressive 2025 campaign that included finishing with a 1.81 ERA.

item.title: Lakers honor longtime PA announcer Lawrence Tanter
item.description: The Los Angeles Lakers honored longtime public address announcer Lawrence Tanter by unveiling a plaque at Crypto.com Arena on Monday, Nov. 23. Tanter spent 43 seasons in that role for the franchise before his death at 76 on Sept. 23 . Tanter had officially retired in June. He had called more than 2,100 games, including 14 NBA Finals series and four NBA All-Star Games, during his tenure. The Lakers played a tribute video during the game that included remarks from Lakers legends Michael Cooper and Mychal Thompson. Fans were also given the opportunity to write messages and memories in honor of Tanter in the Star Plaza outside of the Lakers’ home arena. Lakers coach JJ Redick also shared some thoughts about Tanter before the game against the Utah Jazz on Monday. "He's an iconic voice," Redick told reporters. "He made a mark not only on the Lakers but the NBA." “The first time I ever got to play in Staples Center, the curtains dropped from the scoreboard and the music came on and you hear his voice. … It just felt like I made the NBA. He was an integral part of what made this place so special.” This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Lakers honor longtime PA announcer Lawrence Tanter

item.title: Cricket's saliva ban to stay despite Gill call to overturn rule
item.description: Bangladesh's Shoriful Islam delivers a ball on day one of the second Test in South Africa (PHILL MAGAKOE) The International Cricket Council has no plans to reverse the ban on applying saliva to shine the ball, despite India skipper Shubman Gill's call to allow the practice again. Gill on Monday said the ban should be revoked to help bowlers get reverse swing, after India's high-scoring opening Test in Wellington against New Zealand ended in a draw. However, AFP understands that the ICC has no immediate plans to relax the rule, which is treated in the same way as any other unfair method of changing the ball's condition. Saliva can materially alter the ball when mixed with sweets, chewing gum and mints and the practice is incredibly hard to monitor and regulate. The ICC temporarily barred the practice of applying saliva as a precautionary measure during the pandemic in 2020 and two years later made it permanent. The use of saliva to shine one side of the old ball and keep the other rough helps fast bowlers get the leather ball to swing late. "I don't understand why we haven't been allowed to shine the ball yet -- we are way past Covid times," Gill said after the draw. "There was a rule that you can't put saliva on the ball to make it shine. It's been seven-eight years and I still don't understand why they are not allowing it. "I think this is also a big factor (in bowlers struggling to get wickets)." The tourists had declared their first innings on a mammoth 720-9 midway through the fourth day, but New Zealand survived 120 overs to finish on 239-5 at the close. The Indian Premier League lifted its saliva ban last year, much to the bowlers' delight, but the ICC finds no reason to relax it in international matches. India and New Zealand now head to Christchurch for the second and deciding Test starting Friday, where both captains expect a more typical green, grassy and seamer-friendly wicket. fk/pst

item.title: Houston Astros adding J.P. Martinez, Aaron Bates to coaching staff
item.description: J.P. Martinez (left) and Aaron Bates are the newest additions to the Astros' coaching staff. (Getty Images) In building out their major-league staff under new manager Brad Ausmus, the Houston Astros are hiring coaches J.P. Martinez and Aaron Bates, a person with knowledge of the additions confirmed Monday. Martinez has worked with pitchers, including as Atlanta's bullpen coach last season and previously as a pitching coach for the Giants. Bates spent the past four seasons as co-hitting coach for the Dodgers. The Athletic first reported their impending hires. The Astros have not announced any additions to their coaching staff under Ausmus beyond the hiring of Bobby Wilson as bench coach last week. Last month, the Astros said they planned to retain pitching coach Josh Miller and hitting coach Victor Rodriguez from their 2026 coaching staff. However, that was before the team hired general manager Randy Flores and Ausmus, who was named manager Nov. 11 . Miller will not return to the Astros' staff next season, people with knowledge said Monday. Martinez will reportedly replace him as pitching coach. Rodriguez's status is unclear though he was expected to return to the staff in some capacity as of Monday night. Rodriguez served as Houston's lead hitting coach in 2026 with Anthony Iapoce as assistant hitting coach and Dan Hennigan as offensive coordinator. The Astros did not retain Iapoce after the season. Hennigan left the organization for a job at Wake Forest in August. Martinez, 44, served as Atlanta's bullpen coach last season following five seasons on the Giants' staff as assistant pitching coach from 2021-24 and pitching coach in 2025. Prior to that, Martinez worked for six seasons in the Twins' system, including as a minor-league pitching coach and assistant coordinator. The Astros' pitching staff ranked 24th in the majors in ERA this past season after compiling the American League's lowest ERA from 2021-25. Bates spent 12 seasons in the Dodgers organization, including the past eight on their major-league staff. He was an assistant hitting coach for four years before becoming co-hitting coach. item.title: Commanders pip Bengals in last-gasp thriller
item.description: Washington Commanders kicker Drew Stevens is hoisted aloft by team-mates after his dramatic late field goal clinched victory over Cincinnati (Patrick Smith) The Washington Commanders scored a dramatic 22-20 win against the in-form Cincinnati Bengals on Monday, snatching victory with a Drew Stevens field goal with the last kick of the game. The Bengals looked to be edging towards victory after kicker Evan McPherson nailed a 56-yard field goal with 46 seconds remaining to put Cincinnati 20-19 ahead at the Commanders' Northwest Stadium. But Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels orchestrated a lightning-fast drive from the restart -- which included back-to-back long-range passes to receiver Antonio Williams -- to march the Commanders into field goal range as the clock ran down. Stevens then stepped up to drill a 26-yard field goal to settle an enthralling encounter that sees the Commanders improve to 4-5-1. The Bengals, regarded by many as potential Super Bowl contenders, fell to 7-3. Daniels said he had never doubted his ability to find receiver Williams for the passes of 22 yards and 42 yards that set the Commanders up for the win. "We talk about it in our offensive meeting room, it's all about trust," Daniels said. "I trusted (Antonio) to make a play for us back-to-back and he did." The wild ending was in stark contrast to the Commanders' early offensive struggles, which saw them make just 27 yards on their first four possessions. The Bengals took a 10-0 lead in the second quarter after a Tee Higgins touchdown and a McPherson field goal, before Washington's Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed for a score to make it 10-7 at half-time. A bizarre start to the second half saw the Northwest Stadium field plunged into darkness early in the third quarter when the floodlights went out. ESPN reported that the outage occurred due to stadium officials failing to adjust a regular maintenance schedule which sees the light shut down at 10pm during weekdays. A Stevens field goal leveled the score at 10-10 before Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow tossed his second touchdown of the game, this time to Colbie Young, to put Cincinnati 17-10 ahead. Three unanswered Stevens field goals put Washington 19-17 up before the roller coaster finish saw the Commanders claim victory. rcw/pst

item.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 9: Maxwell Hairston #1 of the Buffalo Bills celebrates after a play during the third quarter against the Minnesota Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium on November 9, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills took care of business against an underdog on Sunday, beating the Miami Dolphins. The Jacksonville Jaguars and Cincinnati Bengals both lost to underdogs from the NFC East on Sunday and Monday, which paves the way for the Bills to clinch the number one seed in a new scenario. Yes, with seven games left it is premature to talk about clinching scenarios, but the Bills have a four-game lead in the AFC East plus two games left against the Jets and Dolphins. The division crown is heavily tilted toward the Bills now, and we are starting to look past that to the one seed. (The Bills are obvously focused one game at a time.) With the Jaguars and Bengals losing this week, the Bills now can win the rest of their AFC games and secure the overall record and the AFC record they would need to clinch the one seed, a status that has eluded them throughout Josh Allen’s entire career. Buffalo has games against the Kansas City Chiefs, Denver Broncos, and New England Patriots plus the Dolphins and Jets. Winning those five AFC contests gets them to 14 wins and an 11-1 AFC record with head-to-head tiebreakers over the Broncos and Chiefs. Denver and KC would both have three losses on account of losing to Buffalo. Meanwhile the Jaguars and Bengals could top out at 14-3 but have two AFC losses apiece. Even in a three-way tie scenario, the Bills would come out on top. In short, if the Bills win the rest of their AFC games, they can lose both games to the NFC North’s Chicago Bears and Green Bay Packers and still be the one seed in the AFC. (Winning those is preferable, but irrelevant here.) If the Bills stumble against an AFC opponent, obviously things will need to be recalibrated. item.title: Rules analyst: Operator should've stopped clock after game-winning FG
item.description: ESPN Monday Night Football rules analyst Russell Yurk said the Cincinnati Bengals could've had two seconds for a kick return if the clock operator had stopped the clock with :02 left in their heartbreaking NFL Week 11 loss to the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium on ESPN's Monday Night Football. The clock continued to run after Drew Stevens' field goal gave Washington a 22-20 lead. "When the ball hit the net, there were still two seconds left on the clock," MNF play-by-play announcer Joe Buck said during the broadcast, shortly after the game ended. "And yet they just evaporated and the game ended." "And that's correct, because the clock ran to zero," Yurk said. "But there were two seconds left when the ball hit the net. So by rule, there were two seconds left. But replay cannot restore time when there are two seconds or more if the next snap is anything other than a scrimmage snap. So because the next snap would've been a kickoff, they cannot by rule put time back on the clock. So it properly ended." "So it ended," Buck replied. "Should the clock have stopped with two seconds left? That's the mistake, right?" "In a perfect world, the clock operator should stop the clock when the ball hits the net. There would be two seconds left for a kickoff. But once it ran to zero, there's nothing replay can do to fix it." Earlier in the game, analyst Troy Aikman pointed out that officials missed a facemask call , in addition to what should have been a roughing call on a late hit of Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow. During the Bengals-Commanders preseason game in 2025, Aikman criticized Bengals defensive back Jordan Battle for not hitting Washington QB Jayden Daniels on the QB's first-quarter touchdown run. The Bengals and Commanders met on Monday night during the 2024 regular season. Buck said it was a must-win game for Cincinnati after an 0-2 start. Washington won 38-33 . item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.)
